rows.old_text: # Slovakia: personal income tax for employees and the self-employed (2026) v1.1
rows.disposition: H1 version aligned with metadata.

rows.old_text: Source-cited draft: not reviewed by an accountant, not for filing. Built by Michael Cutajar and the OpenAccountants team.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: This skill covers the annual income tax of an individual for the 2026 calendar year: employees, the self-employed (SZČO, živnostník) and people with rental, capital or other income. It links to the other Slovakia skills and does not repeat them:
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text:
- [sk-payroll-social](sk-payroll-social.md): the employer's monthly withholding and social and health contributions.
- [sk-corporate-income-tax](sk-corporate-income-tax.md): companies, including the minimum tax for legal persons.
- [sk-tax-overview](sk-tax-overview.md): the system at a glance.
- [sk-cross-border](sk-cross-border.md): residence in detail, non-residents, withholding tax and treaties.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: **Which text of the law.** Act No. 595/2003 Coll. on income tax (zákon o dani z príjmov), version in force from 1 January 2026 to 30 December 2026. Act No. 261/2025 Coll. made the 2026 changes to §11 and §15; under §52zzzj(1) they apply first for the 2026 tax year. A further version in force from 31 December 2026 adds an exemption for informal carers (§9(1)(t)) and amends §11(4), but §52zzzm says those apply first for 2027. Penalties come from Act No. 563/2009 Coll., the Tax Procedure Code (daňový poriadok).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: ## Who this applies to
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text:
- **Residents.** A person with permanent residence (trvalý pobyt) or a home (bydlisko) in Slovakia, or who usually stays there, is taxed on worldwide income (§2(d)(1)). Staying at least 183 days in a calendar year, counting every started day, is usually staying. The tax year is the calendar year (§2(l)).
- **Non-residents.** They are taxed only on Slovak-source income (§2(e), §16). They get the spouse allowance and the child bonus only if Slovak income is at least 90% of their total income (§11(7), §33(9)). The detail is in sk-cross-border.
- **Employees** (§5). The employer withholds monthly advances. An employee with only §5 income from Slovak employers can ask an employer for the annual settlement (ročné zúčtovanie) by 15 February 2027 instead of filing (§38(1)). Otherwise they file DPFO type A.
- **Self-employed** (§6(1) and (2)): trades (živnosť), liberal professions, farmers and other independent activity. They file DPFO type B.
- **Rental income** (§6(3)), **capital income** (§7) and **other income** (§8), such as sale of property, securities or crypto-assets. These go on DPFO type B.
- **Who must file.** Anyone whose taxable income in 2026 exceeds 50% of the personal allowance, so EUR 2,983.37, or who has a tax loss (§32(1)). Income taxed finally by withholding is left out of that test.
- **Out of scope.** Companies, and the special tax on top state officials (§15a).
rows.disposition: Residence/employment/filing routes retained; SK-L01 adds actual DDS settlement exception.

rows.old_text: ## Rates, bands and thresholds
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: The bands and allowances are multiples of the subsistence minimum (životné minimum) in force on 1 January of the tax year (§11(2)(a)). For 2026 that is EUR 284.13 a month, set from 1 July 2025 by Measure No. 168/2025 Coll. Amounts below are that figure times the multiple, rounded to the cent (§47).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: **How the bands work.** The law sets two separate bases (§4(1)). Base (a) is employment income after allowances, plus rental and other income. Base (b) is business income after allowances and losses. Each base is taxed on its own scale in §15(a): base (a) always on the 19% to 35% bands, base (b) at 15% if business revenue is EUR 100,000 or less, otherwise on the same bands.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.
Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: ## The taxable base
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: **Employment (§5).** Gross pay including benefits in kind, minus the employee's compulsory social and health contributions (§5(8)). Pay for 2026 received by 31 January 2027 belongs to 2026 (§4(3)). Withholding and contributions are in [sk-payroll-social](sk-payroll-social.md).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text:
**Self-employed (§6(1),(2)).** Revenue minus either:
- **actual expenses** (preukázateľné výdavky), with tax records or double-entry accounts (§6(11)); or
- **flat-rate expenses** of 60% of revenue, capped at EUR 20,000, if the person is not a VAT payer, or was one for only part of the year (§6(10)). The flat rate covers all expenses except the compulsory social and health contributions, which are deducted on top in the amount paid. The person still keeps a record of income and of inventory and receivables (§6(10), §6(11)(a),(d)).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: The result is the business partial base. A tax loss can be carried forward five years. A micro-taxpayer (business revenue up to EUR 60,000, §2(w)) can use it in full; others only up to 50% of the business base (§30(1)).
rows.disposition: Rechecked current destination; prior 423-unit review disposition: F13 full microtaxpayer gates and5period expiry preserved

rows.old_text: **The 15% rate.** It turns on business revenue under §6(1) and (2), not on profit. Revenue of EUR 100,000 or less gives 15% on the whole business base. Above EUR 100,000 the whole business base goes on the bands (§15(a)(2),(3)).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text:
**Allowances (nezdaniteľné časti, §11).** They reduce only the employment and business bases, never rental, capital or other income (§11(1)).
- The personal allowance and the spouse allowance are tested on the tax base from §5 and §6(1),(2) income. A taxpayer who at the start of 2026 receives an old-age, early, service or similar foreign pension gets no personal allowance if the pension for the year, including the 13th pension, exceeds the allowance; otherwise the allowance is cut to the difference (§11(6)).
- The spouse allowance needs a spouse living with the taxpayer who cared for a minor child, received a care allowance, was a registered jobseeker, or is disabled (§11(4)). The spouse's own income is net of their contributions. Months count only if the conditions held at the start of the month (§11(5)).
- Allowances come off the employment base first, and only the rest comes off the business base (§11(12)).
rows.disposition: Allowance sequence retained and source-backed DDS/PEPP contract/cap/recapture conditions supplied.

rows.old_text: **Rental (§6(3)) and other income (§8).** Income minus proven expenses. Rental income and occasional income are exempt up to EUR 500 in total (§9(1)(g)). Sales of property, movable things, options, securities, shares in an s.r.o. and crypto-assets (§8(1)(b)-(f),(t)) are taxed on the gain. A loss on one type is ignored (§8(2)). Several sales are exempt if held long enough, for example listed securities held over a year (§9(1)(k)). These gains are taxed in base (a) on the bands.
rows.disposition: Rechecked current destination; prior 423-unit review disposition: F04/F05 securities exclusions/proportionalrental/shared500 computation

rows.old_text: **Capital income (§7).** Slovak interest is taxed by withholding under §43 and stays out of the return (§7(3)). Foreign interest and similar income go in a special base taxed at 19% (§15(a)(4)). Dividends from a Slovak company are taxed by withholding. Foreign dividends go in a special base at 7%, or 35% from a non-cooperating state (§51e, §15(a)(5),(6)).
rows.disposition: Rechecked current destination; prior 423-unit review disposition: F03/F14 distinguish governmentbonds/bankinterest/profit-period dividends

rows.old_text:
**Credits.** From the tax computed:
- **Child tax bonus (§33).** EUR 100 a month for each child under 15 and EUR 50 a month for each child aged 15 to 18, for each month at whose start the conditions were met (§33(1),(5)). The child lives in the taxpayer's household, and the taxpayer needs employment or business income. The total is capped at a percentage of the employment or business partial base, or their sum, taken before allowances (§33(6)); the Financial Administration's worked return uses that base. If that base exceeds EUR 27,432, the bonus for each child falls by one tenth of the excess (§33(11)). Only one parent claims (§33(4)). If the bonus exceeds the tax, the difference is paid out (§33(7)). The taxpayer must have at least 90% of income from Slovak sources (§33(9)).
- **Mortgage interest bonus** for borrowers aged 18 to 35 at application (§33a). The conditions differ for loan contracts made up to 31 December 2023 and after; check them in the law before claiming it.
rows.disposition: Full child-credit method and old/new mortgage branches supply the former pointer.

rows.old_text: **Rounding.** Every calculation is to two decimal places, with 5 and above rounded up (§47).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: The extension notice names the new deadline: the end of the month in which the return will be filed. The tax is then due by that new date (§49(3)). The notice is on the Financial Directorate's form.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: A self-employed person registered for income tax, a VAT payer, and any tax adviser or lawyer acting for a client must file electronically (Tax Procedure Code §14(1)). The last known tax for advances is the tax on the business base at 19%, after losses (§34(5)).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: ## Penalties and interest
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: All under the Tax Procedure Code, Act 563/2009, version in force from 1 September 2026. The 1 January 2027 version has the same text for §154 to §156.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text:
- **Late or missing return.** A fine of EUR 100 to EUR 30,000 (§154(1)(a), §155(1)(a)). For a fine within a range, the tax office does not impose one for a first breach (§155(4)). It weighs severity, duration, consequences and the taxpayer's reliability index.
- **Tax understated, found by the tax office.** 3 x the ECB base rate a year, at least 10% a year, on the extra tax, counted daily from the day after the filing deadline. It is at least 1% and at most 100% of the extra tax (§155(1)(f), (2), (5)). Paying within 15 days of the decision cuts it to two thirds (§155(17)).
- **Own correction (dodatočné daňové priznanie).** The ECB base rate a year, at least 3%, on the difference. If filed after a tax audit is announced, within the time allowed, it is 2 x the ECB base rate, at least 7% (§155(1)(g),(h), (5)).
- **Late payment interest (úrok z omeškania).** 4 x the ECB base rate on the day the arrears arose, at least 15% a year, for each day late, for at most four years (§156(2)). It is not charged if it is EUR 5 or less (§156(6)(b)).
- Fines of EUR 5 or less are not imposed (§155(11)).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: ## Cross-border points
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text:
- **Foreign income of a resident.** Include it. Relief follows the treaty: a credit capped at the Slovak tax on that income, or exemption (§45). Including foreign income gives the six-month extension (§49(3)(b)).
- **Non-residents.** Slovak-source income only (§16). The spouse allowance and the child bonus need at least 90% of total income from Slovak sources (§11(7), §33(9)).
- **Withholding** on payments to non-residents, the security deduction and treaty lists are in sk-cross-border.
- **Contributions abroad.** Which country insures a cross-border worker decides which contributions are deducted (§5(8)). See [sk-payroll-social](sk-payroll-social.md).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: ## Worked examples
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: ### Example 1: self-employed on flat-rate expenses
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: Jana is a web designer with a trade licence. She is not a VAT payer. In 2026 her revenue is EUR 48,000. She uses flat-rate expenses and paid EUR 6,000 of compulsory social and health contributions. She has no other income.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: Flat-rate expenses are 60% of EUR 48,000, which is EUR 28,800, capped at EUR 20,000. With the contributions on top, her business partial base is 48,000 - 20,000 - 6,000 = EUR 22,000. That is below EUR 26,083.13, so she gets the full personal allowance of EUR 5,966.73 (21 x 284.13). Her tax base is EUR 16,033.27. Revenue is under EUR 100,000, so the rate is 15%: tax EUR 2,404.99, due with DPFO type B by 31 March 2027. Her last known tax is under EUR 5,000, so she pays no advances in the next period.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text:
```oa-check
name: SK PIT 2026, SZCO flat-rate expenses, revenue EUR 48,000, 15% rate
inputs:
  revenue: 48000
  contributions: 6000
  subsistence_min: 284.13
steps:
  - flat_expenses: min(revenue * 0.60, 20000)
  - partial_base: revenue - flat_expenses - contributions
  - allowance: round(subsistence_min * 21, 2)
  - base: partial_base - allowance
  - tax: round(base * 0.15, 2)
expected:
  flat_expenses: 20000
  partial_base: 22000
  allowance: 5966.73
  base: 16033.27
  tax: 2404.99
```

rows.old_text: ### Example 2: employee with both phase-outs
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: Peter is an employee. His 2026 gross pay is EUR 42,000 and his payslips show EUR 6,000 of employee contributions, so his employment partial base is EUR 36,000. He has one child aged 10 living with him all year. His wife works and does not meet the §11(4) conditions, so there is no spouse allowance. He files DPFO type A.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: The base is above EUR 26,083.13, so the personal allowance phases down: 14,661.11 - 36,000 / 3 = EUR 2,661.11. His tax base is EUR 33,338.89, all in the 19% band: tax EUR 6,334.39.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: The child bonus would be 12 x EUR 100 = EUR 1,200. His base of EUR 36,000 is above EUR 27,432 (1.5 x 12 x 1,524), so the bonus falls by one tenth of the EUR 8,568 excess, EUR 856.80. The bonus is EUR 343.20, well under the 29% cap. Tax after the bonus is EUR 5,991.19, before the advances his employer withheld.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text:
```oa-check
name: SK PIT 2026, employee, allowance phase-out and child bonus taper
inputs:
  gross: 42000
  contributions: 6000
  subsistence_min: 284.13
  avg_wage_2024: 1524
  months_child_under_15: 12
steps:
  - partial_base: gross - contributions
  - allowance_cap: round(subsistence_min * 51.6, 2)
  - allowance: max(0, round(allowance_cap - partial_base / 3, 2))
  - base: partial_base - allowance
  - tax: round(base * 0.19, 2)
  - taper_threshold: 1.5 * 12 * avg_wage_2024
  - bonus_full: months_child_under_15 * 100
  - bonus_cut: round((partial_base - taper_threshold) / 10, 2)
  - bonus: min(max(0, bonus_full - bonus_cut), round(partial_base * 0.29, 2))
  - tax_after_bonus: tax - bonus
expected:
  allowance_cap: 14661.11
  allowance: 2661.11
  base: 33338.89
  tax: 6334.39
  taper_threshold: 27432
  bonus: 343.20
  tax_after_bonus: 5991.19
```

rows.old_text: ## Ask the client first
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text:
1. Where was the client's home and permanent residence in 2026, and how many days were they in Slovakia? Did they have any foreign income?
2. What kinds of income did they have: employment, business, rental, sale of property, shares or crypto, interest, dividends?
3. If self-employed: what was the business revenue (EUR 100,000 test, EUR 60,000 micro-taxpayer test), were they a VAT payer at any time in 2026, and do they want actual or flat-rate expenses? What contributions did they actually pay?
4. Children: dates of birth, months living in the household, and which parent claims the bonus.
5. Spouse: did they live together, which condition in §11(4) applies, and what was the spouse's own income?
6. Did they receive a pension at the start of 2026, pay into supplementary pension (DDS) or PEPP, or have a young person's mortgage?
